items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Launches on Nintendo Switch 2 Next Week, Requiring 117.2 GB of Storage
items.summary: Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 on August 4 with a 117.2 GB file size. Learn about storage needs, microSD Express support and setup checks.
items.content:
Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 on August 4 with a 117.2 GB file size. Learn about storage needs, microSD Express support and setup checks.

Final Fantasy XIV is finally heading to Nintendo Switch 2 next week , but players may need to clear some serious storage space before entering Eorzea.

Square Enix will release Final Fantasy XIV for Nintendo Switch 2 on August 4, giving players another portable way to access its enormous MMORPG. As spotted on the US eShop , the Switch 2 version comes with a hefty 117.2 GB storage requirement.

That is not a minor download by handheld standards. Nintendo Switch 2 includes 256 GB of internal storage, meaning Final Fantasy XIV alone could occupy nearly half of its total advertised capacity. The system software and any games already installed will reduce the space actually available to players, making the practical situation even tighter.

In other words, you may want to begin cleaning out that backlog now.

Nintendo Switch 2 supports microSD Express cards for expanded game storage, and Final Fantasy XIV is exactly the sort of release that makes one worth considering. A 117.2 GB installation leaves considerably less room for other large games, downloadable content, screenshots, and future updates.

Players should also remember that live-service games rarely remain the same size forever. Final Fantasy XIV regularly receives patches, seasonal content, balance adjustments, and major expansions. Its Switch 2 storage footprint could therefore change after launch, even if 117.2 GB is enough for the initial installation.

Standard microSD cards used with the original Switch cannot store and run Switch 2 software. Anyone purchasing additional storage specifically for Final Fantasy XIV should make sure the card uses the microSD Express standard.

Final Fantasy XIV launches on Switch 2 in 4 editions.

The Switch 2 port is still a major step for the game. Portable access could make crafting, gathering, daily activities, and shorter questing sessions more convenient, provided the version delivers stable performance and readable interface scaling.

Final Fantasy XIV launches on Switch 2 next week.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Will Be The Nintendo Switch 2's Biggest Game by Install Size
items.summary: Square Enix MMO Final Fantasy 14 will land on Switch 2 with an almighty thud next month, as its honking install size will take up almost half of the console's 256GB memory.
items.content:
Square Enix MMO Final Fantasy 14 will land on Switch 2 with an almighty thud next month, as its honking install size will take up almost half of the console's 256GB memory.

Final Fantasy 14 will weigh in at 117.2GB when it launches for Switch 2 on August 4, an eShop listing for the title has now revealed. Here's hoping you have space for it — or the budget to buy a new SD card.

That's around double the game's install size on PlayStation 5, which benefits from some clever file compression technology, though similar to the game's memory footprint on PC. It's a hefty download, though perhaps to be expected when you consider the MMO's size and the amount of content that has been added over the years.

The upside to all this is that the filesize includes all of the game's previous five expansions — Heavensward, Stormblood, Shadowbringers, Endwalker and Dawntrail — so you won't need more space to play any of those. The downside? A sixth expansion, Evercold, is already on the way — meaning you'll likely need even more memory space from next January.

Somewhat amusingly, Final Fantasy publisher Square Enix is no stranger to holding the record for the biggest Switch 2 games by memory size. Until the launch of Final Fantasy 14, Square Enix's Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth holds the current record (91.8GB) for a single game, as well as the record for a game bundle (the Kingdom Hearts Collection, which includes a trio of titles that weigh in at 131GB total).

Final Fantasy 14 game director Naoki Yoshida suited up in Bastion armor to take the stage at Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin to confirm the title's long-awaited Switch 2 launch date over the weekend, alongside a laundry list of new updates coming in the near future . The game's first month on sale will be offered without any subscription charge as its servers are stabilized. After this period comes to an end, players will be required to purchase a subscription as normal.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Reactions to Final Fantasy XIV’s second fan festival
"We'd Probably Have To Release Them In 4 Or 5 Instalments" - Final Fantasy XIV's Director On Why More Remakes Haven't Materialised
items.summary: "Look at Final Fantasy VI; it’s such an incredibly huge game."
items.content:
"Look at Final Fantasy VI; it’s such an incredibly huge game."

The Final Fantasy 14 director Naoki Yoshida suggested that if remakes of Final Fantasy VI, VIII, and IX were to happen, they would potentially be a much larger undertaking than the current Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy, requiring four or five instalments (h/t: Genki / VGC ).

Yoshida made the comments during Naoki's Room, an on-stage conversation at the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin , where he was joined by the Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy director, Naoki Hamaguchi, and a pair of translators, with the conversation turning to remakes after the pair were asked for their favourite games.

Through one of the translators, Hamaguchi said this was a discussion he had partaken in with several journalists over the years, regularly answering Final Fantasy VI as one of the most important games he played, but suggested that every time he gave that answer it ends up being misinterpreted as proof he's working on a remake of his own.

"I’ve given this answer to a lot of media interviews," said Hamaguchi. "But Final Fantasy VI is the reason that I wanted to work in games, so that always has a special place in my heart. But every time I give that answer to a journalist or someone, the next day there is an article online saying ‘Hamaguchi will be remaking Final Fantasy VI,’ so I’ll say, ‘No, I am not.’"

It was at this point that Yoshida jumped in and attempted to explain why Square Enix hasn't yet gotten around to remaking these titles, saying that one of the major reasons is the sheer scope of these games and the amount of effort it would take to do it properly.

"Of course, I understand the feelings of the players," Yoshida said. "But you gotta think about it. Look at Final Fantasy VI; it’s such an incredibly huge game. The scale is just immense. And the same applies for other titles like Final Fantasy VIII and Final Fantasy IX. So of course now, since you are working on the Final Fantasy VII series. I do get that people would be asking for remakes of other titles. But if we did remake those other titles, we’d probably end up having to release them in 4 instalments or maybe even 5 instalments.”

In response, Hamaguchi used it as an opportunity to praise the Final Fantasy VII Remake team, crediting them with being a special group due to their loyalty and dedication over the last decade: "I really think, having worked on the Final Fantasy VII Remake series, that I am truly blessed with a wonderful team. They’ve stuck with me for over 10 years, working on three separate games that are remakes of a single game, and there are not many who would do that. We're not quite at the finish line yet. Revelations isn't out, but we're almost there, and I'm so, so grateful to them that we've been able to make it this far."

If you want to watch back the full section, we've included a timestamp here , marking the beginning of this discussion.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Evercold changes housing for the better, Yoshi-P says, and World of Warcraft's "amazing" take on the MMO staple has "been a good source of research"
items.summary: You can expect two changes to Final Fantasy 14
items.content:
You can expect two changes to Final Fantasy 14's housing system to land during the Evercold run of post-expansion patches

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Square Enix) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Final Fantasy 14's housing system is due to get two "very big" overhauls as part of the post-Evercold run of patches, and it looks like Blizzard's own take on the popular MMO feature in World of Warcraft has given Square Enix plenty to chew over.

As part of Final Fantasy 14 Fan Fest in Berlin, producer and director Naoki 'Yoshi-P' Yoshida spoke to the press to tackle some questions about Evercold. Among the most interesting was a question over whether Square Enix had any plans to modernize Final Fantasy 14's housing system.

Speaking through a translator, Yoshi-P jokes that the question may have been refined prior to being presented to him, before adding: "I get the feeling what you really want to ask is, well, WoW has come up with this amazing housing system. How about [Final Fantasy] 14?"

Yoshi-P starts by saying that the Final Fantasy 14 team has an "immense respect" for the World of Warcraft team. And indeed, Y oshi-P has rarely been shy in giving Blizzard its flowers.

Then, he shares that when the Final Fantasy 14 team saw that the WoW devs were working on their own housing system , and that they "looked to [Final Fantasy] 14 and incorporated things which they wanted to surpass us, I think that in itself is very much a sense of great honor for us to hear."

7,000 hours in, Final Fantasy 14 lost me with Dawntrail – but Evercold's changes might win me back Final Fantasy 14 Evercold promises to scrap the MMO's 2-minute meta and change jobs for the better Yoshi-P hoped we wouldn't notice, but Final Fantasy 14 Evercold is inspired by Norse mythology Seemingly happy to return the favor, Yoshi-P says he went "hands-on" with the WoW housing system, and came away impressed and motivated.

"I really do appreciate it. It's amazing," he says. "And we always like taking on new challenges. So this time around, when I tried WoW's housing, I thought it really is amazing, and it's been a good source of research."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The good news is that you'll see the results of that research soon. Yoshi-P says the Final Fantasy 14 team is "planning two very big overhauls for housing" during the patch 8.0 series. If you're averse to numbers, that means it'll arrive at some point between Final Fantasy 14's Evercold expansion launching and whatever the next expansion ends up being.

So what's on the way? Yoshi-P says one of the overhauls relates to the UI as it's currently "quite technical" and "not very accessible." In an ideal world, Yoshi-P would like a casual player to be able to create elaborate housing.

While Yoshi-P can't reveal much about the second overhaul, he does say it will make players happier than the UI update and that it's currently in the planning phase. As such, there's a chance it'll release before the UI update, but we'll just need to wait and see how the chips fall. Yoshi-P says the Final Fantasy 14 team will announce further details when they have more visibility.

The news is the latest sliver we've got about Final Fantasy 14's Evercold expansion. As part of the Berlin Fan Fest, we've also found out that the first new FF14 Evercold job will be a hulking tank called the Bastion, that Final Fantasy 14 is getting a crossover with the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series , and much more. It feels like Final Fantasy 14 is going for it, and that might be just what the MMO needs.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV MMORPG Reveals Bastion Job, New Areas for 'Evercold' Expansion in Videos
items.summary: Guest Creator Mahiro Maeda joins Neon Genesis Evangelion "Ghosts of Desire" collaboration; game
items.content:
The livestream for the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin revealed on Saturday videos for the "Evercold" expansion for Square Enix 's Final Fantasy XIV MMORPG. The videos revealed the new Bastion Job in the expansion as well as new areas available in the expansion.

Additionally, the event announced the game's previously revealed Nintendo Switch 2 version will launch on August 4.

Square Enix will reveal the second new job for the expansion at the Fan Festival event at Makuhari Messe in Tokyo on October 31-November 1.

Square Enix also revealed in the event's keynote speech that the game's collaboration with the Neon Genesis Evangelion series titled "Ghosts of Desire" is bringing on guest creator Mahiro Maeda ( Evangelion: 3.0+1.0: Thrice Upon A Time , Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo ).

Additionally the event revealed a new collaboration with Final Fantasy VII Remake , with a new eight-player raid series that will be featured in the new expansion.

Dive into all the fun of the #FF7R collaboration! 🙌✨ Beyond the Lifestream: Evercold 8-player raid series Keybound Brawler: Gold Saucer typing game There's a lot to look forward to alongside your adventures in Evercold! pic.twitter.com/5bFQe2GfUl

The game's director and producer Naoki Yoshida (also known as Yoshi-P) revealed at the Fan Festival event in Anaheim in April that "Evercold" will begin the series' new "Godless Realms" saga. Players will enter the Fourth, one of 13 reflections of the original Source world. He also teased various creatures including a "Wanderer," Arcane Giants, and a new race of cat creatures. The new expansion will also bring changes, including an updated Adventurer Activity user interface and a more weekly-based system as opposed to daily.

Square Enix released Final Fantasy XIV Online for personal computers in September 2010. After criticism from fans, the company revealed an updated version of the game titled Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn that added a new world and story. Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn launched on Windows PC and PlayStation 3 in August 2013, on PlayStation 4 in April 2014, on PlayStation 5 in May 2020, and on Xbox Series X|S in March 2024.

Square Enix has since released five expansions: "Heavensward" in June 2015, "Stormblood" in June 2017, "Shadowbringers" in July 2019, "Endwalker" in December 2021, and "Dawntrail" in July 2024. The game has recorded just under 35 million registered accounts worldwide as of April 24.

The game's mobile version for iOS and Android devices from Lightspeed Studios launched in China in June 2025, and had planned to have a global launch. However, Square Enix and Tencent announced earlier this month the game will end service in the Chinese mainland on September 30, with the global version seemingly canceled.

Square Enix announced in February 2022 that it will continue support for the MMORPG for the next 10 years.

Source: Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest 2026 livestream

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 has finally added the class I'm always asking for: a Viking with two shields, laser cannons, and Wolverine claws
items.summary: Straight from my middle school sketchbooks.
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Square Enix) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Fantasy RPGs have become too comfortable with delivering the expected gaggle of familiar character concepts. Archers, monks, paladins, you know the drill. I've seen it all before! Give me, I don't know, a Viking that shoots triple-barreled laser guns out of its dual shields, which also have metal claws, you know? Final Fantasy 14 knows what I'm talking about—down to the last detail, in fact.

Watch On Indeed, the first new job to be introduced as part of the Evercold is just that: the bastion, a main tank that blocks, shoots, and stabs all with the same instrument. Those dual weapons, "known as skyltborg," seem to be entirely new to the Final Fantasy setting, though they are reminiscent of Rhitahtyn Arvina 's supersized gunshields. Granted, most of my experience with that setting is through Kingdom Hearts, but I know I would have remembered if Mickey Mouse picked a pair of these up at any point.

The teaser trailer shows off some of its combat animations, and as is FF14 tradition, they're extravagant and accompanied by some badass electronic rock. The roegadyn in the trailer lifts himself into the air to fire laser blasts and uppercut his foe—it looks cool when he does it, but I'm reserving judgment until I've seen how ridiculous a lalafell looks doing all these same animations. Game director Yoshi-P certainly pulled the look off, showing up to the Berlin Fan Festival in full bastion cosplay, as players shared on X .

Notably, the bastion will only be playable in evolved mode, the pruned battle system coming as part of Evercold. More expansion details will come later this year during the Tokyo Fan Festival, and the full thing is set to launch January 2027.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV’s latest live letter gave us a detailed preview of the Beastmaster coming in September
Final Fantasy 14's Evercold expansion brings aboard a Final Fantasy 7 collab and a job that's all about fighting with massive shields
items.summary: And more, more, more, always more than that too.
items.content:
Image credit: Square Enix News by Oisin Kuhnke Contributor Published on July 25, 2026 3 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn - Collector's Edition Finally, a Final Fantasy 14 job made specifically for the type of person who likes to dual wield shields in Dark Souls ! The latest FF14 fan festival is taking place, and with that has come a suite of announcements, including a reveal at one of the two new jobs coming as part of the next expansion, Evercold.

We'll get back to in a moment because I know that someone would try to shoot me if I didn't first talk about the fact that a Final Fantasy 7 Remake themed raid series is also coming to the MMO. It's called Beyond the Lifestream, and it's being made in collaboration with the remakes' writer Kazushige Nojima (who's supervising the story), as well as the ever-mysterious Tetsuya Nomura (who's supervising the art design). Not much was actually revealed about it other than that it will have three full tier raids, and that there'll be outfits available themed around Barret and Tifa.

Right, that new job! It's called Bastion , and it's a main tank role paired with some twin shields. The role does start at level 90, so that's something to keep in mind for newcomers. The vibe really is a bit Soulsy at first glance, up until the role's moves get all magitek-like. That's it on details on the job for now, but plenty more was shown off at the fan festival. For starters there's the plethora of new places to visit, like the incredibly blue-looking city of Fargarth , there's also Naglfar, Realmship of Water , a big ole regal skyship, and Hringhorni, Realmship of Fire , another skyship in which we all must agree to not laugh at the second part of its name.

You can expect a few different system updates too. The team is experimenting with how quests play out, in that some main story quests will be playable in any order, though that won't affect how the story will play out. In tandem, to balance level progression there's a new feature called auto content balancing, which essentially sounds like level scaling catered. There'll be more character creator options like a colour picker for eyes, hair and skin tone, with more planned further down the line. And the new combat overhaul, Evolved, will also be coming, with a stream planned to take place at a later date detailing how it differs from the original system, Reborn (which you'll still be able to use).

There's a lot more than that too, so you can check out the broadcast to see all the finer details.

items.content: Beginning Tuesday, April 28, with the release of Patch 7.5, the free trial will also include the award-winning FINAL FANTASY XIV: Shadowbringers. Spread the word and tell your friends, because there’s never been a better time to begin their adventure! Check out the free trial. For those who have already registered FINAL FANTASY XIV: A Realm Reborn to their accounts, worry not─this change also applies to all existing owners as well. * Service accounts will be updated to reflect this change starting on Tuesday, April 28. Please note that the registration status update may not be displayed immediately on the Mog Station.
